nodes.gadka_ok.text.t: "A pilgrimage, you say. To Beckby, for your uncle's health." The older one scratches his beard. "Lucky uncle, to have a nephew like you. Go. And stay out of our way, because next time I might not find it so funny." They leave.

nodes.gadka_test.options.[gadka_t].text.t: Speak firmly and look them in the eye.

nodes.gadka_test.text.t: The scouts give you a sullen look.

nodes.gadka_zle.text.t: "A pilgrimage? With a sword on your belt and hilt calluses on your fingers? Poor uncle, with a nephew who lies that badly." The younger one scratches something on a wax tablet. "We'll remember. And you remember you saw us." They leave, and you feel their eyes on your back for a long while after.

nodes.kontrola.options.[gadka].text.t: Spin them a tale about a pilgrimage.

nodes.kontrola.options.[lapowka].text.t: Give them twenty groats to leave you be.

nodes.kontrola.options.[schowaj].text.t: Slip into the cellar under the tavern.

nodes.kontrola.options.[stoj].text.t: Stand still and let them search you.

nodes.kontrola.options.[stoj_zle].text.t: Stand still and let them search you.

nodes.kontrola.options.[stoj_znowu].text.t: Stand still and let them search you.

nodes.kontrola.text.t: Two men in red cloaks stop you mid-stride. One runs his eyes over your boots, the other over your mug. "Name. Where from. Where to. Who vouches for you?" Grumble the innkeeper stands in the tavern doorway, pretending he doesn't know you. Out of the corner of your eye you see a little door behind the barrels that you'd never noticed before.

nodes.lapowka.text.t: The older one weighs the purse in his fist and shrugs. "Twenty. Not much, but enough for us not to see your mug for an hour. One hour." They head off towards the tavern, and Grumble pulls a face like somebody just paid him back a debt.

nodes.obszukaj_ok.text.t: The scouts rummage through your bag and pockets without ceremony. Nothing, unless you count a gap-toothed comb. "Clean," the older one mutters, without much interest. "Go. And watch yourself, because these days clean means suspicious." They leave.

nodes.obszukaj_zle.text.t: The younger scout pulls the rolled-up insignia of the tribute party out of your bag and holds it up to the light like a fish he's just landed. The older one says nothing, then gives a crooked smile. "School of the Blade. Well, look at that. What luck." It ends with you running across the yard, cowering in a dark corner, sure that worse is coming. The scouts don't give chase, but they write it down.

nodes.obszukaj_znowu.text.t: The older scout doesn't even look in your bag. "You again. School of the Blade, we remember. We're not checking this time, we know what we'd find. Remember, you're on our list." They walk off slowly, so you can see they could have stayed.

nodes.papiery.text.t: The older scout turns the scrap of paper in his fingers, holds it to the light, sniffs it and hands it back. "Dirty seal, but a seal. Go on, only don't lose it, or next time I'll be asking whose seal it is." They walk off, and for a while longer you hold your breath.

nodes.schowaj.text.t: Before the scouts finish the question, you're behind the barrels and through the little door. The cellar stinks of sauerkraut and mouse droppings. You sit there for over two hours, with footsteps thudding and voices rumbling overhead. At last it goes quiet. Grumble lifts the hatch. "They're gone. But remember, I'm not your mother."
